newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's May M2 money supply up 18.9 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's May M2 money supply up 18.9 pct yr/yr.

text.p: South Korea's M2 money supply rose 18.9 percent in May year-on-year, against a 15.3 percent rise a year earlier, the Bank of Korea said on Friday.
NOTE: M2 consists of money in circulation, checking account and savings account deposits with banks. MCT consists of M2, certificates of deposit (CD) and money in trust accounts.
A Bank of Korea official said the stronger M2 growth in May compared with a year ago was a result of the extension in May last year of the maturity on trust accounts.
The maturity change has led to a shift of a large amount of deposits from trust accounts to savings accounts in banks.
But the MCT growth lagged in May due to a sharp drop in issuances of covered bills and depository products, a statement from the central bank said.
Loans that banks extended in May declined to 4.37 trillion won from 5.36 trillion a year earlier due to a sharp slowdown in banks' lending growth, it said.
Long and short-term money market rates dropped sharply in May from the previous month on the back of slower corporate demand for funds.
The overnight call rate slipped to 11.73 percent at end-May from 14.16 percent a month earlier, while benchmark three-year corporate bond yields fell to 11.9 percent from 12.5 percent.

Yields on three-month certificates of deposit (CD) declined to 12.24 percent at end-May from 13.10 percent at end-April, while yields on commercial papers (CP) dropped to 12.58 percent from 13.59 percent.
